newsitem.title: UK: Copper surge halted, aluminium firm in late LME.
newsitem.headline: Copper surge halted, aluminium firm in late LME.

text.p: A sudden rush higher in copper prices, to the day's highs, in evening inter-office trading was halted before 1900 GMT when prices had slipped back again.
"You have to expect volatility after such a sharp rise recently," a trader said. "It was thin," he added.
There was probably some option covering going on as the market's rise took the cash metal price close to $2,400 where there is a large option open position, traders said.
The three months price after edging close to $2,250 a tonne slipped back to be quoted at $2,225/$2,230 at 1900 hrs.
Aluminium extended its gains strongly after it moved above a a long term trendline extending back to August 1995, and also breached the 100-day moving average.
Traders said this triggered investment fund buying and shortcovering and some far forward buying interest was also noted.
At 1900 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,478/$1,480 a tonne.
